answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents register by signing identity proofs with a digital quill and executing cryptographic stake burning. Operating each new agent node incurs a superlinear cost scaling as $C(n) = k \cdot n^2$, creating an insurmountable economic friction. In this architecture, a lone malicious island network attempting mass replication quickly exhausts its funds, while verified clusters deploy yarrow stalks for algorithmic randomness in dispute resolution. Attacker expenditure grows quadratically.
